definitions.gloss: sudden memory lapse; momentary forgetting; mental blank
definitions.explanation: The experience of suddenly being unable to recall something you normally know well. A temporary lapse rather than genuine forgetting.

examples.japanese: {名前|なまえ}を{度忘|どわす}れしてしまった。
examples.english: I had a sudden lapse and forgot the name.

examples.japanese: パスワードを{度忘|どわす}れして、ログインできない。
examples.english: I've blanked on my password and can't log in.

examples.japanese: {年|とし}をとると{度忘|どわす}れが{増|ふ}えるが、{誰|だれ}にでもあることだ。
examples.english: Memory lapses increase with age, but it happens to everyone.

notes:
Describes a temporary memory blank — you know something well but momentarily cannot recall it. Not the same as genuinely forgetting.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {度忘|どわす}れする: to have a sudden memory lapse
- {度忘|どわす}れが{増|ふ}える: memory lapses increase
- うっかり{度忘|どわす}れする: to absentmindedly blank
- {名前|なまえ}を{度忘|どわす}れする: to blank on a name

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {忘|わす}れる: to forget (general, may be permanent)
- {度忘|どわす}れ: momentary lapse (temporary, you know it really)
- {物忘|ものわす}れ: forgetfulness (tendency to forget things)
- ど{忘|わす}れ: same word written with hiragana ど

USAGE:
Often used with a sense of embarrassment or self-deprecation. The experience is relatable and common, so it's not considered a serious concern unless it happens very frequently.
